title: Atrial fibrillation: type, history and anticoagulation
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's atrial fibrillation and related long-term drug therapy.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of atrial fibrillation.

HPI
The patient is a 73-year-old male who presents today for a scheduled follow-up regarding his atrial fibrillation. He reports that his heart rate has been well-controlled over the last month. He denies any palpitations, lightheadedness, or shortness of breath during daily activities. He notes that he feels generally well and has been able to maintain his usual level of exertion. He is currently managed with a rate-control medication strategy. He is not currently prescribed any anticoagulant medication due to his low risk profile.

Review of Systems
The patient reports no chest pain, no shortness of breath, and no syncope. He denies any recent falls or generalized weakness. He denies any changes in vision or speech. He reports no joint pain or significant changes in appetite.

Social History
The patient lives at home with his wife. He retired five years ago and enjoys gardening and walking. He denies tobacco and alcohol use.

Family History
His father had a history of hypertension and a mother who had a history of coronary artery disease.

Medication List
- Metoprolol 50mg daily
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Vitals
BP: 128/82 mmHg
HR: 72 bpm (regular)
RR: 16 breaths/min
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 98% on room air

Recent Labs
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2
HbA1c: 6.4%
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L

Exam
The patient appears in no acute distress. He is alert and oriented x3. Chest is clear to auscultation. Heart sounds are regular with a rate of 72 bpm. No murmurs are noted. Lungs are clear. Extremities are well-perfused with no edema.

Assessment
1. Atrial fibrillation: The patient’s heart rate remains stable on his current beta-blocker regimen. He denies symptoms of tachycardia.

Plan
1. Atrial fibrillation: Continue current rate-control medication. We will continue to monitor his heart rate and rhythm during our regular visits.
2. Follow-up: The patient will return to the clinic in three months for a routine evaluation.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, NP, 05/14/2026
explanations: Current atrial fibrillation without a documented type: I48.91 (HCC 238).

distractors.why: The provider does not document the type.
The atrial fibrillation is current (treated and monitored).
